newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Grain - Market focus on world sales.
newsitem.headline: Australian Grain - Market focus on world sales.

text.p: Australia will be chasing international wheat sales in the coming week with tenders out from a range of buyers, especially Pakistan.

After striking a 200,000 tonne sales deal with Egypt last week, Australia would be bidding for the Pakistan tender of more than 225,000 tonnes, Alex Nichol of the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) told Reuters.
"It'll be interesting to see how the AWB fares (on the Pakistan tender)," one independent industry source said. "They wished they'd sold more wheat earlier in the week to Egypt."
The AWB had not fared as well as hoped in the Egypt deal because of price, he said.
The Pakistan tender for 225,000 tonnes to 270,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat would appear most likely to go to a combination of Australian and U.S. wheat, on the specifications.
But brokers and analysts said that with Argentina throwing out strong price competition and Pakistan a price-sensitive market, the outcome was unpredictable.
The NSW storage and handling group expects that the record will not last long. And quality remains good, traders said.
But, with a big harvest on one side and a gradual awakening of international wheat demand on the other, the Australian physical and cash market remained quiet last week.
One private trader reported that sales were going mostly to the AWB pool, leaving the cash market quiet with prices firm.
Guy Allen of GrainCorp also said farmer selling was less than expected during the week. "They've been fairly tight holders."
Other buyers lining up in the international marketplace include Turkey, Algeria, Sri Lanka, Bulgaria, Bangladesh and Mozambique, the AWB and brokers said.
"There's a fair bit of business around," Nichol said.
"This is the demand everyone's been waiting for for months but nobody's buying any more than they absolutely have to," Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures said.
Australia's wheat harvest poured a record million tonnes of grain into New South Wales (NSW) storage facilities of co-operative GrainCorp in the week to last Tuesday.
Prices strengthened mid-week with AH delivered Newcastle trading A$174 to A$178 a tonne. ASW feed wheat into Newcastle was quoted at A$148-A$152 with trades earlier in the week at A$155.
Private traders saw domestic cash ASW prices firming by A$2.00-A$3.00 over the week, with the Newcastle cash price ending the week at A$148 to A$150 -- on few trades.
Bill Mitchell of New England Agricultural Traders said cash prices firmed during the week especially for premium wheat, underpinned by the AWB pool price and on Chicago's earlier bounce.
Cash prices for Prime Hard Moree firmed by up to A$10.00 on a best bid basis.
"A lot of people are holding on to wheat, which will limit the prospect of a sustained rise post-harvest, there'll be plenty around for sale," he said.
Over the past week, AWB indicator prices for ASW in the main centres were steady or up by A$1.00 to A$2.00 a tonne.

Futures prices firmed slightly over the week in near-term contracts but drifted back in more distant contracts as prices remained stuck in their range and brokers looked for a decisive move one way or the other.
